name: OJBench
description: OJBench is a competition-level code benchmark designed to assess the competitive-level code reasoning abilities of large language models. It comprises 232 programming competition problems from NOI and ICPC, categorized into Easy, Medium, and Hard difficulty levels. The benchmark evaluates models' ability to solve complex competitive programming challenges using Python and C++.
typical_sota_score: ~15–35% (frontier models as of 2024–2025; problems are Olympiad-level)
reputation: One of the hardest coding benchmarks; problems from prestigious NOI (National Olympiad in Informatics) and ICPC; designed to stress-test frontier coding models on competition-level algorithmic problems
notes: Problems sourced from NOI (Chinese National Olympiad in Informatics) and ICPC (International Collegiate Programming Contest). Evaluated on Python and C++ separately (see also OJBench-CPP). Problems require advanced algorithmic knowledge including dynamic programming, graph algorithms, data structures, and mathematical insight.
